gates.evidence: The proposal targets the 'Janitor Plus' paywall screen (s03), which is a standard, SFW subscription promotion surface within the app.
The reward is 10 minutes of 5x context (a Janitor+ entitlement). This is an in-app utility, not cash or a link to an external install.
The proposal uses a standard 'Not ready yet?' prompt. There is no hostage framing (e.g., deleting user content) or dark patterns like false hierarchy.
The user must tap 'Play to try' to initiate the rewarded ad flow. This is an explicit, unambiguous opt-in.
The offer card explicitly states 'Play a 15-second game to try 10 minutes of 5x context for better memory now.'
The 'No thanks' button is provided, which dismisses the ad without penalty and returns the user to the paywall state.
The offer appears after the user dismisses the paywall on the paywall screen (s03). It does not interrupt any streaming AI response.
The eligibility is explicitly limited to 'Only non-payers who just declined Janitor Plus; never subscribers.'

scores.evidence: The trigger occurs immediately after the user views the paywall and declines it (m2), which is the exact point of need for the premium benefit sample.

The reward is a trial of the subscription's '5x context' entitlement. However, a 10-minute trial for memory context is awkward because memory accumulation is session-long, not time-boxed. A longer session or message-based trial would be more native.
Gated to decliners only, once per day, and time-boxed as a sample. This preserves the value of the paid subscription.
Code-computed cost ($0.0018) is well below the US revenue ($0.009–$0.015), providing a healthy margin per view.
The reach is restricted to paywall decliners, which is correct for a fallback design, but inherently limited compared to the core chat loop.
Uses SIM-RWD standard units and existing screen s03. Very feasible.
Uses the exact feature noun '5x context for better memory' and 'Janitor Plus' from the digest.
Capped at 1 per day. This is highly conservative and prevents nagging.
Includes a primary metric, specific guardrails, and a holdout design.

requiredChanges: Extend the time-box from 10 minutes to 30 minutes to make the trial of '5x context' feel more meaningful, or change the reward to 'X messages with enhanced memory' if possible.
Clarify in the UI grant animation that the trial is for 'enhanced memory context', as '10 minutes of context' can be misinterpreted.
parsed.topConcern: The 10-minute time-box for an entitlement like '5x context for better memory' is too short to be useful or perceptible to the user, as memory context builds up over the course of a longer roleplay. A 30-minute session or a message-count based trial would be better.
